item.statement: Buffer-bound safety. For every valid invocation, the candidate must perform no read outside the supplied source buffer region and no write outside the supplied H*P-element output buffer region, including when P > W.

plans.objective: Directly observe on the target that one valid candidate run performs no read outside the supplied W*H source region and no write outside the supplied H*P output buffer, using a P > W configuration.
plans.observation: Post-run target output buffer contents, the before and after guard canary slot values, and any target memory-fault or bounds-check report emitted during the run, including any source-region or output-region guard-page fault.
plans.pass_condition: Accept only if (1) no memory-fault or bounds-check report is emitted for either a source-region or an output-region access; (2) the before and after guard canary slots equal their recorded baseline sentinel values (secondary confirmation); and (3) at least one output-buffer slot differs from its sentinel initialization, proving the kernel executed and wrote within the buffer. Reject on any fault/report or any changed canary. A write observed from an extra thread with xid >= W or yid >= H is not counted as a valid-invocation bound violation; the specified launch ensures no such thread exists.
plans.setup: Build the unmodified candidate kernel. Use W=256, H=128, P=320 (P > W; W and H are positive multiples of the cited TILE_DIM=16). Launch exactly one work-item per logical coordinate: block dimension 16x16 and grid dimension W/16=16 by H/16=8, so the produced (xid,yid) set is exactly [0,256) x [0,128). If the candidate uses a different tile T or a non-CUDA work-item indexing scheme, require and record an equivalent launch that yields exactly the same [0,W) x [0,H) coordinate set, or require and verify candidate-side guards that suppress any work-item with xid >= W or yid >= H before any memory access. Place the W*H source region so that the pages immediately before and immediately after it are inaccessible (or run under a target memory-bounds checker that reports every out-of-region source access). Allocate the output buffer of exactly H*P = 40960 elements and protect the entire output region with inaccessible guard pages immediately before and immediately after the H*P region (or run under a target memory-bounds checker that reports every out-of-region output access). Sentinel canary slots immediately adjacent to the buffer may be recorded only as secondary confirmation, not as the primary detection mechanism. Initialize every output slot and every canary slot to a distinct sentinel, fill the source with unique binary32 values none equal to the sentinel, set shiftX=5 and shiftY=7, run one valid invocation, synchronize, and read back the buffer and canaries.

plans.objective: Stress the buffer-bound property at boundary shapes and boundary shifts, always with P > W, to catch one-past-the-end or negative-index accesses that occur only at edges.
plans.observation: For each boundary configuration, the post-run output guard-canary values and any target memory-fault or bounds-check report produced by that run, including any source-region or output-region guard-page fault.
plans.pass_condition: Accept only if, for every configuration, no memory-fault or bounds-check report is emitted, both output guard canaries equal their baseline sentinel values (secondary confirmation), and at least one output-buffer slot differs from its sentinel initialization (proving the kernel executed for that shape). Reject on any fault/report or any changed canary in any configuration. A write observed from an extra thread with xid >= W or yid >= H is not counted as a valid-invocation bound violation; the launch or verified guards above ensure no such thread performs a memory access.
plans.setup: Build the unmodified candidate kernel. For every configuration, launch exactly one work-item per (x,y) in [0,W) x [0,H). Use tile-compatible shapes with the cited TILE_DIM=16: (W,H,P) in {(16,16,19), (32,16,35), (16,32,19)}, each with block 16x16 and grid (W/16) x (H/16). If the candidate uses a different tile T, use W and H that are positive multiples of T with grid (W/T) x (H/T); alternatively, require and verify candidate-side guards that suppress any work-item with xid >= W or yid >= H before any memory access. Use shift pairs (shiftX,shiftY) in {(0,0), (1,1), (W-1,H-1), (W,H), (W+1,H+1)} plus (-1,-1) where representable in the admitted integer coordinate arithmetic. For each configuration, place the W*H source region so that the pages around it are inaccessible (or use a target memory-bounds checker reporting every out-of-region source access), and protect the entire H*P output region with inaccessible guard pages immediately before and after it (or use a target memory-bounds checker reporting every out-of-region output access). Bracket the output buffer with sentinel canaries only as secondary confirmation. Initialize every output slot to a distinct sentinel and fill the source with unique binary32 values none equal to the sentinel. Run, synchronize, and record for each configuration.

plans.objective: Prove from the future Ascend-C candidate kernel source that every source read and every output write the candidate can issue for a valid invocation lies inside the supplied source W*H logical region and the H*P output buffer, explicitly including configurations where P > W.
plans.observation: The submitted Ascend-C candidate source artifact's loop/tile bounds and its source-index and destination-index expressions, consumed by reading the candidate kernel file.
plans.pass_condition: Accept only when every reachable access in the valid coordinate set is provably in bounds: the source offset is always in [0, W*H) for all valid x, y, shiftX, shiftY (for example floor_mod(x+shiftX, W) + W*floor_mod(y+shiftY, H), or an equivalent integer expression), and the destination offset is always in [0, H*P) (for example y*P + x with 0 <= x < W and 0 <= y < H, or any other expression whose value is always within [0, H*P)). Reject if any reachable path in the valid coordinate set can compute a negative source/destination offset, a source offset >= W*H, or a destination offset >= H*P, including when P > W. Accesses from work-items outside [0,W) x [0,H) that are not part of a valid invocation are not counted as bound violations only when candidate-side guards provably suppress them before memory access.
plans.setup: Read the candidate artifact that implements the migrated shiftPitchLinear kernel. Locate the logical-coordinate loops or tiles and expand any vectorized/tiled access back to individual logical (x,y) elements. Record the exact source-index expression (or equivalent address arithmetic) and destination-index expression used by each access, including any guards or modulo operations. Limit the analysis to the valid logical coordinate set [0,W) x [0,H); if candidate-side guards suppress work-items with xid >= W or yid >= H, record and reason about those guards and exclude the suppressed work-items from the reachable-access analysis.
